newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN MINISTRY SAYS UNEMPLOYMENT TO FALL FASTER.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN MINISTRY SAYS UNEMPLOYMENT TO FALL FASTER.

text.p: Zero growth in the fourth quarter of 1996 marked only a temporary flattening in Germany's economic recovery and the pace of expansion should pick up during the current year, the Economics Ministry said on Friday.

A ministry report described the surge in unemployment in January to nearly 4.7 million, the highest since 1993, as a cause for "great concern". But it said that a large element was seasonal and would fall away faster than usual during the spring.

In extracts from its February monthly report, the ministry said construction activity in the fourth quarter had picked up, but a lull was now expected after tax changes which encouraged builders to bring projects forward to late 1996.
"As a result, we can expect a decline in building output in the coming months, and in addition awards of new building contracts fell back nationwide in the fourth quarter," it said.
The ministry said fourth quarter economic output was not likely to be higher than in the previous quarter, and was two percent above a year earlier.
But it said the interruption to growth was likely to be "only temporary". The Bundesbank on Thursday estimated fourth quarter gross domestic product unchanged.
Weakness was seen across a range of economic indicators, including the Ifo index of business confidence, manufacturing orders and industry capacity utilisation, the ministry said.
The report made no mention of a strong pickup in business sentiment in January reported on Thursday by the Ifo institute, whose widely-watched index for west Germany jumped to 93.3 from 90.9.
Problems on the jobs market were exacerbated by a cold January and a change in state payments for idle construction workers which contributed to half a million more workers signing on unemployed.

"Even if one assumes that the January unemployment result clearly overstates the underlying trend, and as a result there should be a faster than usual fall in seasonal share of unemployment this spring, its high level is a cause for great concern," the report said.

The retail price situation in Germany remained relaxed after the turn of the year, with the 0.5 percent rise in January against December caused mainly by temporary factors -- like a jump in heating oil prices which has since reversed.

Dollar strength has pushed up the price of raw material imports, but strong competition and weak domestic demand has meant that no significant price rises have been passed on to the consumer. Unit labour costs continue to fall, it said.
